description: Converted guild, noble, and pirate origins.

entries.title: Guild Artisan of the Sky Trade Origin
entries.summary: A converted origin for recognized craftspeople whose reputation and livelihood are tied to a sky-trade guild.
body: Sky-trade artisans manufacture, repair, certify, and sell the goods that keep airborne communities alive. Their guild identity can be as important as nationality.
Membership brings standards, competitors, debts, workshops, suppliers, and professional expectations. A guild can provide shelter and opportunity, but it also remembers disgrace.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 origin package
body: Associated skills: Craft (chosen trade) and Diplomacy. These are always class skills for the character.
Origin focus: Gain a +2 origin bonus on Craft checks in the chosen guild specialty and on Appraise checks involving products of that trade.
Trade specialty: Choose one Craft specialty appropriate to a recognized sky trade. Profession (merchant) may be substituted for characters trained primarily as factors or brokers.
Starting package: A set of artisan’s tools, a guild certificate or seal, a ledger, work clothing, sample materials worth 10 gp, and 15 gp.

Access feature — Guild Connections: In a settlement where the guild operates, the character can usually identify a guildhall, approved workshop, supplier, or reputable lodging place. Access to facilities, credit, restricted materials, or labor still requires payment, reputation, sponsorship, or a successful social check.

sections.heading: Character creation use
body: Select this origin at 1st level as the character’s single origin package. It does not consume a feat or replace ancestry or class features.
The GM may replace individual pieces of starting gear with setting-equivalent items of roughly equal value.
The origin’s access feature creates a credible route to information, shelter, audiences, or facilities. It does not guarantee cooperation or eliminate payment, law, reputation, or risk.

entries.title: Skybound Noble Origin
entries.summary: A converted origin for heirs and retainers of island rulers, fleet-owning houses, and families tied to Dragon Lord courts.
body: Skybound nobles inherit names, obligations, political enemies, and access to institutions that ordinary travelers cannot easily reach.
The origin may represent a ruling heir, an impoverished scion, a political hostage, a household officer, or a relative whose family prestige is real but conditional.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 origin package
body: Associated skills: Diplomacy and Knowledge (nobility and royalty). These are always class skills for the character.

Origin focus: Gain a +2 origin bonus on Diplomacy or Knowledge (nobility and royalty) checks involving recognized noble houses, Dragon Lord vassals, court protocol, hereditary claims, and formal audiences.
Trade specialty: Choose Profession (courtier), Profession (administrator), or one additional language used in regional diplomacy.
Starting package: A signet ring or authenticated crest, court clothing, writing materials, a letter of lineage or appointment, and 25 gp.

Access feature — Noble Influence: Where the character’s house is recognized, they can request an audience with a minor official, guild leader, estate officer, or noble retainer. The request normally secures consideration within 1d4 days, not compliance. Hostile houses may instead use the request to locate or pressure the character.

entries.title: Guild Apprentice Origin
entries.summary: A converted origin for current and former apprentices trained within a guild workshop or professional organization.
body: Guild Apprentices carry the habits, terminology, standards, and grudges of formal training even when they never completed it.
An apprentice’s strongest assets are usually practical fundamentals and a network of people who remember their mentor, workshop, or unfinished obligations.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 origin package
body: Associated skills: Craft (chosen trade) and Knowledge (local). These are always class skills for the character.
Origin focus: Gain a +2 origin bonus on Craft checks in the trained specialty and on Gather Information checks made through workers, apprentices, or guild contacts.
Trade specialty: Choose one Craft specialty or Profession tied to the former apprenticeship.
Starting package: Apprentice-quality artisan’s tools, guild insignia, a training ledger, work clothing, raw materials worth 5 gp, and 10 gp.

Access feature — Guild Affiliation: In a settlement where the guild or a related trade operates, the character can seek bench space, basic advice, or introductions to journeymembers. Ordinary workspace may be available at a modest daily fee; restricted facilities require sponsorship or proof of standing.

entries.title: Pirate Origin
entries.summary: A converted origin for current and former sky raiders, smugglers, prize crews, and outlaws known in pirate ports.
body: Kaysender pirates survive through audacity, shipboard skill, violence, reputation, and knowledge of settlements where official law has limited reach.
A pirate origin does not require an evil alignment. It can represent a deserter, privateer, forced crew member, rebel raider, smuggler, or former Black Fleet sailor.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 origin package
body: Associated skills: Bluff and Climb. These are always class skills for the character.
Origin focus: Gain a +2 origin bonus on Intimidate or Knowledge (local) checks involving pirates, smugglers, outlaw ports, captured vessels, and black-market crews.
Trade specialty: Choose Profession (air sailor), Profession (navigator), or Use Rope.
Starting package: Pirate clothing, a raid trophy, 50 feet of rope, a grappling hook, a concealed knife, and 8 gp.

Access feature — Raider’s Reputation: In an outlaw port or among active raiders, the character can usually identify a fence, crew broker, safe drinking house, or person willing to hear a proposal. Hospitality is not free, and enemies, bounties, or rival colors can turn recognition into immediate trouble.
